name: Gibbon
tagline: time mode flies on its own tethers; space mode swings and slices on two
summary: Round 2, after Garrett's review: two modes. TIME mode feels like flying: the Gibbon plants its own anchor prisms ahead, alternating sides, and yanks itself along them on short elastic tethers (the Tether prototype's auto-tethers). Squeeze a trigger and you are in SPACE mode: each trigger fires its own tether and its stick aims it, then reels it. One tether is a swing round its anchor, two is a bolas round the line between them, none is a fling through space until time mode takes the sticks back. Every tether is a light sword: what it sweeps through, it cuts.

spec.v: auto-tethers every 0.35 s, 0.8 s ahead, 20° off the nose
LT + left stick = left tether · RT + right stick = right tether
reel 40 u/s, spin limit 0.6 rev/s, +20% past a half turn, cap 358

fantasy: A brachiator in space. It never flies straight for long: it hooks the world and swings through it, and the mass other pilots lay is its forest canopy.
why: Grapple and swing is the second hottest movement verb of 2024-26 (Spider-Man 2 at 11M+, Marvel Rivals' most-loved heroes are its swingers, Echo Point Nova 98% positive). The forgiveness rules come from Echo Point Nova: a target is remembered for half a second after you looked past it, and the rope lets go on its own when it stops making sense.

charge.name: Blade
charge.tip: A proposal (the Tether's): Charge is the blade. Its cutting width grows; at level 5 a beam cuts shielded prisms outright instead of popping the shield.

mass.name: Anchor
mass.tip: A proposal: Mass is the anchors' size. At level 5 a rival's prism you swung off becomes yours when you let go.

space.name: Reach
space.tip: The Tether's proposal: Space is how far a tether reaches.

time.name: Reel
time.tip: The Tether's proposal: Time is how fast a stick reels its tether in.

styles.name: Acrobat
styles.info: Long reach and a fast reel: chains swings far apart.

styles.name: Slicer
styles.info: A wide blade and big anchors: flies through mass cutting it.

styles.name: Maxed
styles.info: Every element at 10. A ceiling, not a match state.

rows: no trigger: the sticks fly, the auto-tethers pull you along on the beat; ghost rings mark what each trigger would hook
a trigger held: its stick aims that tether (W A S D left, arrows right), then stick up reels in, down lets out · one tether swings, two make a bolas · the hull follows the rope
let go of every trigger: you fly on, the sticks still aim; time mode takes the sticks back after the fling (1.6 s) · squeeze again to chain

notModelled: The Tether prototype's long tether aims with a SEARCH PLANE that roll tilts; here each tether aims with its own stick (Garrett's space mode). The stick aim is the studio's proposal: neutral points ahead and out on its own side.
Two tethers (the bolas) are new here: the hull keeps both ropes rigid and orbits the line between the anchors. The Tether in Unity holds one long tether at a time.

The blade never cuts the course ribbon (it is the course) or this hull's own prisms; shields pop and survive that contact, as the Rhino sword's rule. Super-shields, crystals as hook targets and the hook RPC are not modelled.
Auto-anchors stay in the world as in the game, but the studio keeps only each hull's last 150.
Charge and mass MODES (Garrett: later) are not here; the element rows are proposals until Garrett signs them off.
sources: Design: Docs/Studios/CONCEPT_FLEET.md sections 8.1 (the merge) and 9 (Garrett's review, 2026-10-17). Unity side: Assets/_Scripts/Controller/Vessel/R_VesselActions/TETHER.md, AutoTetherRig.cs and TetherMath.cs on cece/loving-feynman-hlgf18; the numbers are TetherConfig.asset's.
